course_description: Introduction to the mathematics of computer graphics and 3D visual computing. Topics include coordinate frames, vector mathematics, primitive rasterization, 2D/3D affine transformations, projection frustums, lighting models (Phong), shading techniques, texture mapping, and OpenGL programming with GPU pipeline optimization.

course_outcomes.co_description: Implement primitive geometric rendering algorithms and coordinate transformations using graphics libraries.
Formulate mathematical projection matrices and evaluate GPU rendering pipeline bottlenecks.
Evaluate lighting and illumination models (Phong, Blinn-Phong, Gouraud) for real-time visual realism.
Design and synthesize interactive 3D graphical applications incorporating texture mapping and user input events.
Demonstrate professional collaborative practices and code documentation in computer graphics team development.

weekly_schedule.topic: Course Orientation, Syllabus Review, and Graphics Systems Architecture

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain the course learning objectives and graphics hardware roles
Install and configure IDE with graphics libraries (OpenGL/GLFW)
Acknowledge the academic integrity policy and software engineering rigor

weekly_schedule.topic: Mathematics of Graphics: Vector Spaces, Points, and Coordinate Frames
weekly_schedule.teaching_learning_activity: Mathematical Problem Solving and Lab Demo

lesson_outcomes.description: State mathematical properties of dot products, cross products, and matrices
Write functions calculating vector normalizations and transformations
Appreciate mathematical rigor in visual computing

weekly_schedule.topic: Primitive Geometry Generation and Bresenham Line/Circle Algorithms

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe rasterization concepts and scan conversion mechanics
Implement line and circle drawing algorithms programmatically
Value algorithmic efficiency in low-level rendering

weekly_schedule.topic: 2D Transformations: Translation, Scaling, Rotation, and Homogeneous Coordinates

lesson_outcomes.description: Formulate 3x3 homogeneous transformation matrices
Construct composite transformation routines in code
Demonstrate precision in matrix multiplication orders

weekly_schedule.topic: Viewing in 2D, Clipping Algorithms (Cohen-Sutherland), and Window-to-Viewport

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain Cohen-Sutherland outcode tests and viewport mapping
Apply clipping algorithms to boundary geometries
Display diligence when debugging boundary clipping conditions

weekly_schedule.topic: Preliminary Examination: Theoretical and Hands-on Practical Exam

lesson_outcomes.description: Recall fundamental math and primitive rendering theories
Execute live timed transformation coding problems
Exhibit professionalism and honesty under timed assessment
Differentiate 2D versus 3D affine transformation matrices
Program 3D translation, pitch, yaw, and roll rotations
Exhibit meticulous attention to gimbal lock considerations

weekly_schedule.topic: Projections: Orthographic vs. Perspective Viewing Frustums

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain field of view (FOV), aspect ratio, and projection planes
Compute view matrices for movable synthetic cameras
Value user visual comfort in virtual camera placement

weekly_schedule.topic: Polygonal Meshes, Normal Vectors, and Hidden Surface Removal

lesson_outcomes.description: Analyze Z-buffering algorithms and face-culling techniques
Calculate surface normal vectors for triangle meshes
Appreciate resource optimization in polygon management

weekly_schedule.topic: Illumination Principles: Ambient, Diffuse, and Specular Reflection

lesson_outcomes.description: Formulate vectors for Lambertian diffuse and specular highlights
Code basic color modulation reflecting light source distances
Display curiosity in physical optical approximations

weekly_schedule.topic: Shading Models: Flat, Gouraud, and Phong Interpolation

lesson_outcomes.description: Contrast per-vertex versus per-fragment normal interpolation
Implement Phong reflection model shaders
Commit to visual fidelity versus computational trade-offs

weekly_schedule.topic: Midterm Examination: Practical 3D Camera & Shading Project Evaluation

lesson_outcomes.description: Synthesize 3D transforms, camera views, and lighting concepts
Demonstrate working 3D scene rendering under inspection
Defend technical architecture decisions before evaluators

weekly_schedule.topic: Texture Mapping Foundations: UV Coordinates and Texture Sampling

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain UV unwrapping, mipmapping, and bilinear filtering
Map 2D texture images onto 3D geometric surfaces
Value aesthetic craftsmanship in asset integration

weekly_schedule.topic: Advanced Texturing: Normal Mapping and Alpha Blending

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe tangent space normal mapping and transparency blending
Code fragment shaders computing perturbed surface normals
Show patience in debugging transparency rendering order

weekly_schedule.topic: User Interactivity, Mouse Raycasting, and Event-Driven Animation

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain screen-to-world raycasting and event queues
Integrate keyboard and mouse camera steering loops
Foster user-centric thinking in interactive interface design

weekly_schedule.topic: Graphics Engine Optimization: Framebuffer Objects and Draw Call Batching

lesson_outcomes.description: Analyze GPU pipeline bottlenecks and draw call overheads
Profile frames per second (FPS) and optimize vertex buffers
Uphold performance excellence in high-demand rendering

weekly_schedule.topic: Capstone Graphics Project Integration and Peer Playtesting

lesson_outcomes.description: Structure full interactive graphics engine components
Collaborate on multi-module codebases using version control
Practice constructive peer critique and team accountability

weekly_schedule.topic: Final Examination & Capstone Defense: Formal Evaluation

lesson_outcomes.description: Synthesize all graphics programming theories and practices
Present and defend functional 3D graphical software solution
Demonstrate Perpetualite professional leadership and ethics
